name: Aerospace mounting bracket (GE jet engine bracket challenge, 2D slice)

load_cases.name: Vertical
load_cases.reason: GE / GrabCAD Jet Engine Bracket Challenge (2013) load condition 1: 8,000 lbf vertical = 35,600 N

load_cases.name: Horizontal
load_cases.reason: challenge load condition 2: 8,500 lbf horizontal = 37,800 N

load_cases.name: Angled 42 deg
load_cases.reason: challenge load condition 3: 9,500 lbf at 42 degrees from vertical = 42,300 N (fx = 28,300 N, fy = 31,400 N)

warnings: Envelope 178 x 65 mm and pad positions are to confirm from the challenge STEP file.
The challenge's torsion load (load condition 4, 5,000 lbf-in) is out-of-plane: noted, not checked in 2D.

safety_factor.original_text: SF 1.5 (standard aerospace ultimate factor, FAR 25.303, to cite)

notes: 2D slice of a known benchmark (original ~1.8 kg Ti-6Al-4V, winner ~80% lighter); not comparable to the 3D challenge results.
This is a 25 mm thick 2D slice that carries the full challenge load. The real bracket is wider at the base, so stresses here are several times those in the real part.
The four 0.375-24 base bolts (interfaces 2-5) are merged into two pad pairs in the side view; each pad stands for the two bolts behind each other along the viewing axis.
Original material: Ti-6Al-4V, yield 131 ksi (about 903 MPa) at 75 F; minimum wall 0.050 in (1.27 mm).
references: GE / GrabCAD Jet Engine Bracket Challenge page (2013): load cases, 0.75 in clevis pin, 0.375-24 bolts, Ti-6Al-4V, min wall 0.050 in, STEP file. https://grabcad.com/challenges/ge-jet-engine-bracket-challenge

Carter, W. T., et al. (2014), The GE Aircraft Engine Bracket Challenge: An Experiment in Crowdsourcing for Mechanical Design Concepts, Solid Freeform Fabrication Symposium: original mass about 1.8 kg, winner about 80% lighter.
